newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU transport ministers to tackle truck charges.
newsitem.headline: EU transport ministers to tackle truck charges.

text.p: European Union transport ministers are due on Tuesday to look at how much money trucks should pay in tolls and fees for using motorways in the 15-country bloc, EU diplomats and officials said.

Talks will centre on a plan drawn up by the Dutch EU presidency to set rules governing charging systems in each EU country, including the "Eurovignette" circulation tax used in Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Luxembourg and the Netherlands.

The Dutch have proposed six annual maximum fees for trucks using motorways, ranging from 690 European currency units ($780) to 1650 ecus depending on how much the lorries pollute and on how much damage they do to roads.
The current Eurovignette maximum is 1250 ecus a year.
Ministers must reach unanimous agreement on the proposal, because it concerns tax issues, a result which is far from certain given the divisions thrown up in preparatory meetings.

Germany and Austria want higher charges than those proposed, suggesting a 2,000-ecu upper limit, one EU diplomat said, while Spain, Greece, Ireland, the Netherlands and Portugal meanwhile, see the proposed figures as "excessive".
Spain and Greece, along with Italy and Portugal, also want to be allowed to set taxes down to half the minimum rates set out in the proposal.

Disagreement also remains about the duration and eligibility for the half-price "Eurovignette" fees currently levied on trucks registered in Greece, Ireland and Portugal when they travel on motorways of countries applying that system.
Spain wants the same discount for its trucks on account of its distance from the centre of the EU, an argument which has prompted Britain, Italy and Finland to cry "us too".

If the Dutch presidency solves those questions, it will still have to tackle a problem raised by Austria, which wants to retain the current tolls charged on its Brenner Pass route to Italy even though they break EU rules requiring that fee levels be linked to infrastructure costs.
Austria says it needs the higher tolls to curb the diversion of trans-Alpine freight onto its roads because of Switzerland's truck-weight limits and transit restrictions. ($=0.88 ecus)
